bug_semantics: The ext_in upload rule accepted the MIME-derived guessed extension without checking the client-provided filename extension. Consequently, GIF content uploaded as shell.php could satisfy ext_in[avatar,gif]; if an application then called move($path) into a web-accessible executable directory, UploadedFile preserved the attacker-controlled original filename and the PHP payload could execute.
flaw_origin: Commit 2bd4f8f5053d97715d5ad320e08cac7ef20da104 first added FileRules::ext_in and made its allow-list decision with UploadedFile::getExtension(). In that same tree, UploadedFile::getExtension() returned Config\Mimes::guessExtensionFromType($this->getType()), so the new rule validated a MIME-derived extension rather than the client filename. The immediate parent f3d286b9e6ac38d39cdd1ef5c59742e34fe3a1b3 contains no ext_in rule.

CVE.org API record CVE-2026-48062 is PUBLISHED and states that versions < 4.7.3 are affected and v4.7.3 fixes ext_in checking the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension.

git show 2bd4f8f5053d97715d5ad320e08cac7ef20da104:system/HTTP/Files/UploadedFile.php shows getExtension() returning Config\Mimes::guessExtensionFromType($this->getType()), proving the BIC's ext_in value was MIME-derived.
git show f3d286b9e6ac38d39cdd1ef5c59742e34fe3a1b3:system/Validation/FileRules.php plus an exact ext_in search returns no ext_in rule, directly verifying parent-tree absence.

At tag v4.7.2, system/Validation/StrictRules/FileRules.php still checks only $file->guessExtension(); UploadedFile::guessExtension() derives from getMimeType(), while its constructor sets name/originalName from the client filename and move($targetPath) defaults to getName(), preserving shell.php.

git show 29299349e7d232e9532767c7cefaed30957309be shows the direct fix in system/Validation/StrictRules/FileRules.php: it lowercases getClientExtension(), rejects empty or disallowed client extensions, and rejects a mismatch between guessExtension() and clientExtension; regression tests cover GIF content named shell.php.

reasoning: The advisory's exploit depends on a mismatch between trusted content-derived type and the untrusted original filename. The initial ext_in implementation in 2bd4f8f5053d97715d5ad320e08cac7ef20da104 introduced exactly that mismatch by accepting getExtension(), which was already MIME-derived in the same commit tree, while its direct parent had no ext_in rule. Later refactors and the explicit guessExtension spelling did not originate the mechanism. The vulnerable BIC predates and is contained by affected releases through v4.7.2. Direct fix 29299349e7d232e9532767c7cefaed30957309be binds the client extension to the allow-list and to the guessed extension and first ships in v4.7.3. Because the BIC commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI marker or trailer, the closed BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI.
